shared_elements: circles or discs arranged in a row low on the surface
vertical/horizontal linear bands dividing the surface into registers
rectilinear framed panel in the upper area
rounded or arched upper contour of the stone
justification: Both are upright stones whose decorated face is organised into stacked registers, with a bordered rectangular panel of repeating pattern above and a row of discs/circles set lower down, which is the most specific correspondence. The difference is decisive in execution and form: A is a bulky three-dimensional monolith with deep, rounded, partly figural relief and a body-like silhouette, while B is a flat arch-topped slab with shallow, ruler-straight incision and a purely geometric lattice, giving no sense of a shared hand or intent.
